title: Towards Robust Pseudo-Label Learning in Semantic Segmentation: An Encoding Perspective (ECOCSeg)
mechanism: Replace one-hot classes with error-correcting output codes and denoise labels bit by bit, so partly wrong pseudo-labels cost only some bits.
adaptation: Design bits shared across our 24 classes (dark defect, thin, structural, metal). A crack vs inactive confusion, where 20% of crack pixels sit in inactive regions, then costs one bit. Also usable with jittered GT in the supervised house model.
min_experiment: House PF with an ECOC head vs a one-hot head, 5 seeds. Metrics: crack IoU, inactive IoU, mIoU_rob. Kill if n.d.
evidence: R: plugs into existing UDA and SSL methods with gains across architectures; numbers not on the abstract page.
prior_overlap: Multi-label and structured heads are on the 'never tried' list. Open.

alt_notes.adaptation: Encode the 24 classes so related classes share bits (crack and inactive share a defect bit; busbar, ribbon and splice share a metallisation bit). This gives a multi-label-like head and a softer penalty for crack-versus-inactive confusion where the labels overlap.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: house with a 32-bit ECOC head, 5 seeds. Baseline: house. Metrics: crack IoU, inactive IoU, mIoU_rob. Kill: all three n.d.
